applicant_utility.summary: You never apply for this Fellowship directly: you submit an NUS PhD application through GradApp and your faculty or department decides whether to nominate you, so the real work is building a PhD application strong enough for a faculty to champion. International students receive the lowest stipend tier (SGD 3,900 a month) but the only one-off benefits - an S$1,000 settling allowance and up to S$750 for a single economy airfare - and both are forfeited if you miss the one-month claim window after travel. The tuition waiver is complete, but the award does not promise to meet all your expenses, so plan for the gap between the stipend and Singapore living costs. Treat nomination as an uncertain outcome inside your admissions cycle rather than a guaranteed second funding stream.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Research-strong PhD applicants with a clear project and a faculty willing to nominate them, particularly international candidates who want a tuition-free NUS doctorate.
application_readiness_checklist: Identify the faculty or school you are applying to and read its own application deadline, since the Fellowship has no central deadline
Build the four compulsory items to nomination standard: GPA record, statement of purpose, referee letters and CV
Contact academic or professional referees early so letters speak directly to research potential rather than generic achievement
Sit the GRE if you can - the page treats strong quantitative, verbal and analytical scores as a significant strengthener
Keep every airfare receipt and invoice, and file the PGF Claim Form within one month of the date of travel
common_rejection_risks: A weak or generic statement of purpose that does not connect research interests, career aspirations and motivation to the specific NUS programme
Referee letters that describe classroom performance instead of independent research capability
No faculty advocacy: a competitive application that no department chooses to nominate never reaches the University's selection
No GRE and no publications, when competing candidates have both and the page calls them significant strengtheners
Late airfare claims that forfeit the settling and travel allowances after the money has already been spent
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Anything beyond the tuition waiver and the SGD 3,900 monthly stipend (international rate): housing, food, transport and personal costs above that stipend, plus any travel beyond the single one-off airfare. The NUSGS Research Incentive Award's monthly allowance is not quantified on the official page, so it should not be budgeted as a known figure.
document_audit: The airfare claim needs the official PGF Claim Form plus receipts or invoices, emailed to gradenquiry@nus.edu.sg with the exact subject line format - a mislabelled email can stall the claim
Referees must be academic or professional and able to comment on research potential, not personal character
The CV is compulsory and should foreground publications and research involvement, even though those items are listed as optional
The signed letter of undertaking is required of successful applicants, so read the terms and conditions before signing
alerts: There is no scholarship deadline to chase and no direct application: nomination by the faculty is the only route, and each faculty sets its own admissions deadline
International students admitted from AY2014/2015 owe 312 hours of teaching duties under the Graduate Assistantship Programme, which is time taken out of research
Outcomes arrive in May for August admission and October for January admission, so do not assume funding is confirmed before you commit to the intake

No bond is attached to the Fellowship; the page states 'No specific bond requirements', but the page warns that all information is subject to change and the Research Incentive Award allowance can be revised by NUSGS
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: GradApp PhD application with scholarship indicated -> Faculty/Department nomination -> University selection -> notification in May or October -> letter of undertaking.

applicant_utility.summary: There is no separate scholarship form to fill in: NUS assesses you for this award from your undergraduate admission application, so your admissions application and interview are the scholarship decision. The package is full subsidised tuition, S$5,800 a year for living costs, S$5,000 a year for accommodation and a one-off S$1,750 computer allowance, but accepting it means taking the MOE Tuition Grant, which bonds permanent residents and international students to three years of work for a Singapore-registered company after graduation. Renewal is not automatic - you need a GPA of at least 3.5 every semester, or top-80% cohort standing in Dentistry, Law and Medicine. Treat the bond and the GPA condition as the real cost of the award, not the paperwork.
applicant_utility.best_fit: School-leavers with strong results plus a genuine leadership and co-curricular record who intend to work in Singapore after graduating and can accept the Tuition Grant bond.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are applying as a freshman to a full-time degree - transfer applicants are explicitly excluded
Identify your qualification group's admissions window and pay the application fee before the closing date, since payment must land by that date
Prepare evidence of leadership and co-curricular achievement alongside academic results, since both are stated criteria
Model the MOE Tuition Grant bond, plus the five- or six-year Ministry of Health service bond if you are admitted to Dentistry or Medicine, before you accept
Check that you hold no other scholarship, fellowship, bursary, grant, award or allowance, unless the University has approved it in advance
common_rejection_risks: A co-curricular or leadership record that is thin relative to academic results, when the criteria require all three
Applying as a transfer applicant from a local or overseas university, which is outright ineligible
Missing the shortlist email for the interview because it went to a spam folder - only shortlisted applicants are contacted
Letting the cumulative GPA fall below 3.5 (or out of the top 80% of the cohort in Dentistry, Law and Medicine) after enrolment
Holding a second concurrent award without prior University approval, which breaches the terms and conditions
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The non-refundable NUS application fee (S$10, or S$20 for international students with international qualifications), any tuition above the subsidised rate, and living, housing, travel and personal costs beyond the S$5,800 living and S$5,000 accommodation allowances. Dentistry and Medicine students additionally carry Ministry of Health service bonds of five and six years.
document_audit: Only one application form per applicant, and only one fee payment - duplicate or multiple payments are non-refundable
Supporting documents must be uploaded through the Applicant Portal; an incomplete submission is stated to affect the outcome
Applications submitted with an incorrect qualification type will not be processed, so the applicant group choice is a hard gate

IB, Gaokao, HKDSE, Indian Standard 12 (CBSE and ISC) and STPM candidates must update final results within 3 calendar days of release

Accepting means taking the MOE Tuition Grant and its three-year Singapore work bond even though the scholarship itself carries no bond
